Let that sink in. **After:** > Shared drafts are out today.

What I did: > > - Came up with the idea on my own, before I knew any similar plugins existed. > - Gathered the outside research on similar plugins that shaped the design. > - Decided what the plugin should do, reviewed the work, and edited this README. Claude has two usage limits: one resets every 5 hours, the other every week. When you get close to one, this plugin makes Claude stop at a good moment and save a note (Claude calls it a "handoff") about where it left off, and give you a resume prompt to copy. After the limit resets, you paste the resume prompt into a new chat session and Claude carries on. ## How this plugin helps - You don't lose work halfway. Without it, Claude can hit the limit in the middle of a change and leave files half-edited, with no record of what it was doing. - A fresh chat uses less of your new limit. Claude's short-term memory of a chat (the "cache") runs out after an hour, so continuing the old chat after the reset makes it re-read the whole conversation at full

# Levels Levels is a set of seventeen skills for Claude Code. Each layer skill rates one part of a project (interface, backend, tests, security and so on) on a scale from 1 to 5, shows what is missing for the level you choose, and proposes options. If you ask it to build, it splits the work into small sub-plans and hands them to cheaper models, after showing you the plan and asking first. ## See it run
